findings.what: No test caught an account listed for one registered service being taken as proof of another registered service. Mutant (outside the checkout): requester's check rewritten to `if _, listed := services[deref(e.Subject)]; listed && e.Kind == "pod" && e.Service != nil { service = *e.Service }` -- i.e. any listed account trusts the launcher's claimed service. With it, go test ./internal/broker/requests ./internal/broker/api ./internal/broker/policy ./internal/broker/config ./internal/broker/e2e all ok, and cmd/broker's TestOneServicesTwoAccountsEachGetItsSecret passed; the mutant granted other-service's OTHER_KEY to a pod running as example-service's account under other-service's launcher, and SERVICE_KEY to a pod running as other-service's account under example-service's launcher.

proof.surface: Real compiled broker binary (go build ./cmd/broker at head) started by hand against a Postgres Job + ClusterIP Service in the cluster, fake secrets file with SERVICE_KEY owned by example-service and OTHER_KEY owned by other-service.
proof.command: $TMPDIR/t354/run.sh ./broker-head "example-service=<A> example-service=<B>" (env: productionEnv equivalents, BROKER_FAKE_SECRETS_FILE, BROKER_DATABASE_URL on the cluster Postgres); then GET /healthz and POST /v1/secrets/{SERVICE_KEY,OTHER_KEY}/reread. Also newline/tab-separated "example-service=<A>\n\texample-service=<B>\nother-service=<D>" and today's one-account-per-service "example-service=<A> other-service=<D>".
proof.observed: broker listening; healthz 200; SERVICE_KEY {served:true}; OTHER_KEY {served:false, reason owner-tag-malformed} (other-service unregistered, so the loader got the service names, not the accounts). Mixed-whitespace and today's shapes: listening, both secrets served.
proof.negativeControl: Base binary 5c182bd16f0a, same configuration: EXIT 1 before listening, `BROKER_SERVICES must give each service once, got "example-service=system:serviceaccount:example-other:example-worker-b"`.

proof.criterion: Line 2: a configuration naming one account twice is still refused, with a message naming the account.
proof.surface: Real compiled broker binary started by hand, as above.
proof.command: run.sh ./broker-head with BROKER_SERVICES = "example-service=<A> example-service=<A>"; "example-service=<A> other-service=<A>"; "example-service=<A> example-service=<B> other-service=<D> example-service=<A>" (repeat not adjacent); BROKER_SERVICE_LOGINS naming the service's second pod account B; BROKER_SERVICE_LOGINS naming another service's pod account; the default account as a second account.
proof.observed: Each EXIT 1 before listening: `names the service account system:serviceaccount:example:example-worker-a twice for "example-service"; each account proves one service, so name it once` (adjacent and non-adjacent); `... for both "example-service" and "other-service"; ...`; `BROKER_SERVICE_LOGINS names system:serviceaccount:example-other:example-worker-b, the account BROKER_SERVICES binds for "example-service"'s pods ...`; same for other-service's account; `names a namespace's default service account`.
proof.negativeControl: Same run with the two accounts distinct starts (proof 1). Base binary on "A twice" refuses with the old wording `for both "example-service" and "example-service"`, which the new same-service wording replaces.

proof.criterion: Line 3: a pod under any of a service's accounts obtains its secrets; a pod under none does not, and gets no approval path -- including an account listed for a different service, and an account dropped from the configuration.
proof.surface: Real compiled broker over HTTP via the repository's real-process harness: local OIDC issuer, real projected pod tokens, token logins, pod enrollments, cluster Postgres.
proof.command: cd packages/envoy && go test ./cmd/broker -run 'TestOneServicesTwoAccountsEachGetItsSecret|TestAnAccountProvesOnlyTheServiceItIsListedFor' -v -count=1; plus a throwaway real-binary scenario (outside the checkout): pods A and B granted, a 20-request concurrent burst from both, then a second broker on the same database with BROKER_SERVICES listing only A.
proof.observed: Two services with own logins (example-service on A,B; other-service on D): other-service's pod on D granted OTHER_KEY; pods under other-service's credential running as A or B, and a pod under example-service's credential running as D, each denied SERVICE_KEY and OTHER_KEY with decision deny, grant_id/record_id/approver null (6 denials). Burst: 20/20 granted. After restart without B: pod A values 200 SERVICE_KEY=service-value and new request granted; pod B's held grant values 403 GRANT_NOT_LIVE 'the current policy no longer allows SERVICE_KEY', new request denied, record_id null, approver null.
